# CONFORMANCE

The conformance ID register of `rule30-api`. Every id has exactly one scenario in
`features/suites/<suite>.feature`, tagged with the id and its level, and the evidence
`model/ledger.toml` names; `bin/r30 api check` refuses drift between them.

The three honesty levels (R2):

| Level | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `some-true` | A fact reproduced from an authority (here: a refuted route, from its Lean refutation or experiment). **Not established here.** |
| `build` | Constructed here and validated against its oracle (the Lean kernel, `lexlean verify`, `api check`). Evidence, not a proof. |
| `open` | Measured and reported. **Never asserted.** |

| `route-d-lhcolagree-coboundary` | `some-true` | Route A of the 2026-11-01 reading: under a center period, settledness of the zero diagonals z, z+2 at two scales forces the left half's column -1 to agree across the lag (LhColAgree), so the conditional refutation not_centerPeriodic_of_lhColAgree_one_scale_step_doubles fires. | register: refuted (Rule30UOR.Interfaces.not_periodic_lhColAgree_one_of_doubles) |
| `left-transient-above-diagonal` | `some-true` | Target 1 of the 2026-11-01 reading: the minimal transient of the left diagonal d exceeds d for every d >= 8, so the center (t, t) is never in the settled left region. | register: refuted |
| `single-row-agreement` | `some-true` | Route B of the 2026-11-01 reading: under a center period, the prefix and tail spatial agreements (hpref, htail) of the driven right half rhCenter in one row at scale 2^L hold, so the conditional refutation not_centerPeriodic_of_two_scale_single_rh_row_prefix_and_tail_settleBound fires. | register: refuted (Rule30UOR.DoublingDepth.two_scale_single_rh_row_engine_hypotheses_unsat) |
| `driven-left-cone` | `some-true` | A left half-line driven from white by an eventually periodic boundary has an eventually periodic Pascal cone at column 0 (which, with the increment law and masked Jen, would contradict a center period). | register: refuted |
| `driven-right-column` | `some-true` | A right half-line driven from white by an eventually periodic boundary has an eventually periodic column +1 (which, by the recombination and Jen's adjacency theorem, would contradict a center period). | register: refuted |
| `increment-law` | `build` | The center's increment is Jen's masked column plus the left half's own Pascal cone: center (t+1) XOR center t = (cell t 1 AND NOT center t) XOR coneZero t for every t, where coneZero is the Pascal cone of the left run-ends at positions <= 0. Hence, by masked Jen (prize kit), under any center period P the left half's cone coneZero is not P-periodic from any start. | frontier check: Rule30UOR.Antidiagonal.center_increment_all kernel-checked under propext and Quot.sound and published |
| `black-time-consistency` | `open` | No eventually periodic boundary with black times is black-time consistent: if a boundary column c with c 0 = true satisfies c (t+1) = NOT (column -1 of the left half it drives) at every black time t, and is eventually periodic, it is eventually white (NoPeriodicBlackConsistent). This left-only statement implies Problem 1. | register: open (Rule30UOR.DiagonalCone.NoPeriodicBlackConsistent) |
| `duhamel-and-tails` | `build` | Duhamel form of the rule: every cell is the seed's Pascal transport plus the Pascal cone of the run-end sources (cell_eq_seedAt_bxor_coneAt); the light cone splits by left diagonal into a head of finitely many eventually periodic diagonal cones (period 3 2^d from 2^d) and a tail (problem1_iff_leftTail); the block cone form (problem1_iff_noBlockConePeriod); and the Mahler form of periodicity (a word is periodic iff its Mahler coefficients vanish above a degree; towerWord's Mahler degree). | frontier check: Rule30UOR.ColumnCone.cell_eq_seedAt_bxor_coneAt kernel-checked under propext and Quot.sound and published |
| `single-seed-mask` | `build` | The left-only obligation is exactly the single-seed mask: NoPeriodicBlackConsistent iff SingleSeedMask (no eventually periodic boundary with infinitely many black times is black-time consistent with the left half it drives from the unit seed). With it, the kit's period-two question decides the obligation's period-two slice, and the obligation implies the zero-state center is aperiodic (NoZCenterPeriod). | frontier check: Rule30UOR.UnitSeedMask.noPeriodicBlackConsistent_iff_singleSeedMask kernel-checked under propext and Quot.sound and published |
| `isolated-black-slice` | `build` | The obligation restricted to boundaries whose black times are isolated holds exactly when no walled arithmetic progression exists (NoPeriodicIsolatedBlackConsistent iff not WalledAP), and the obligation implies that restriction. | frontier check: Rule30UOR.Walled.noPeriodicIsolatedBlackConsistent_iff kernel-checked under propext and Quot.sound and published |

| `conditional-audit` | `build` | bin/r30 audit reads, in one Lean introspection of the research library, every theorem concluding not CenterPeriodic T P, Problem1 or not CenterPer T P (or False under a CenterPeriodic hypothesis), identifies each hypothesis beyond the period and the arithmetic side conditions by its head, and classifies the conditional refutation dead (a hypothesis refuted under a period by a named theorem), live-discharged (every hypothesis discharged and the composition kernel-checked in Lean) or open (the hypotheses neither refuted nor discharged); --write records it in model/audit.toml and Audit.lex.tex, whose kernel-decided theorems are that every dead entry names a refuting theorem, the statuses are declared, the theorem names are distinct, and the count of each status; claim --related lists the open hypotheses of the conditional refutations a claim concerns. | bin/r30 audit; bin/r30 verify api --modules src/Audit.lex.tex; scripts/tests/test_audit.py AuditTests.test_classification_of_recorded_statements_conditional_audit |
| `induce-phase` | `build` | The saved round workflow .claude/workflows/rule30-round.js opens with an Induce phase before Propose: one agent runs bin/r30 discover --window 256 --degree 2 --json and bin/r30 audit --json (a missing command is reported and contributes nothing) and returns the observed relations not in the register and the open audit obligations, which every lens receives as context and which enter Refute and Mechanize as proposals of their own (an observed relation is a candidate theorem for all t whose window certificate is already decided); the view publishes the workflow. | scripts/tests/test_audit.py RoundWorkflowTests.test_the_round_opens_with_the_induce_phase_induce_phase |

## discovery

| ID | Level | Statement | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `discovery-basis` | `build` | Sequences.lex.tex declares the basis of the map: 79 sequences of the paper's notions (the constant, the time and trailing parities, the ruler background, the center, the cells at positions -8..8, the right and left diagonals and the tower words j <= 12, the exposed masks k <= 8, the masked column, the two cones and the seven ledger diagonals), each with its lexeme, Lean constant, parameters and κ-label (sequence <lexeme> <parameters>), and its window for t < 512 evaluated from the host Lean definitions by bin/r30 sequences --write in one Lean file that proves every evaluation form equal to its host constant; the kernel decides that the ids and the κ-labels are distinct and that every window has 16 words below 2^32, and api check refuses data that is not the basis or whose labels are not the labels of its entries. dyadicRow, blockParity and wittRespBool are excluded, with the reason recorded. | bin/r30 sequences --write; bin/r30 api check; lexlean verify rule30-api; scripts/tests/test_r30.py DiscoveryTests |
| `relation-search` | `build` | Discovery.lex.tex declares the contract RelationSearch (input a window of chunked Nat bit-vectors, output masks over the sequences; precondition IsWindow, postcondition AllRelationsHold, each with an executable validator and a soundness theorem), the realization RelationEngine (Gaussian elimination over F2 with a mask per pivot), the model RelationSearchModel, the transforms of the extended basis (shift, even and odd dilations, AND) as data, and the kernel decides on 64 times of the real data that the engine finds the edge parity, the left light cone, the cone identity cone-zero = cell(-1) and the increment law in the basis, and that its output passes the postcondition. | lexlean verify rule30-api; bin/r30 api check; scripts/tests/test_r30.py DiscoveryTests |
| `recurrence-search` | `build` | Discovery.lex.tex declares the contract RecurrenceSearch (input one window as bits, output a connection polynomial with leading 1; precondition IsSequenceWindow, postcondition SatisfiesRecurrence: the recurrence holds for every L <= t < N), the realization RecurrenceEngine (Berlekamp-Massey over F2) and the model RecurrenceSearchModel; the certificate is the recurrence on the window, not its minimality; the kernel decides s(t) = s(t-2) for the time parity and the tower word 2 and s(t) = s(t-3) for the period-3 word 100. | lexlean verify rule30-api; bin/r30 api check; scripts/tests/test_r30.py DiscoveryTests |
| `discovery-roots` | `build` | The production roots buildColumns, findRelations and findRecurrence of Discovery.lex.tex are executable, admit the allocation, overflow and recursion effects on rust-std, and apply their models through checked_apply with both the precondition and the postcondition checked at run time, so every output is accepted by a validator the kernel proved sound; they are requested beside the roots of Api and Rule30Core in production/request.json and runtime-roots.toml. | bin/r30 api production; bin/r30 api check; scripts/tests/test_r30.py DiscoveryTests |
| `discover-command` | `build` | bin/r30 discover [--window W] [--degree 1|2] [--write] runs the engines on the basis (the certified Rust of the roots when they are built and cargo runs them, otherwise the Python mirror re-checked by the mirror of the validators, and says which), reports every relation with its columns, κ-label (relation <sorted column labels>), class (register, trivial, consequence, new) and certificate (the rank before its dependent column), and the recurrence of every base window; --write appends the new relations to the register as status observed. | scripts/tests/test_r30.py DiscoveryTests; bin/r30 discover --window 256 --degree 2 |
| `observed-status` | `build` | The register has the status observed: a relation certified on a window (relation, window, κ-label), re-validated by frontier check against the committed windows and refused when it does not vanish; Register.lex.tex carries every claim's relation and κ-label and decides that every observed claim has both; Discovery.lex.tex decides that every relation of the register vanishes on its window; the Observer counts an observed claim as neither a real quality nor withdrawn, and the site renders its mark. | bin/r30 frontier check; scripts/tests/test_r30.py DiscoveryTests |
| `discovery-candidates` | `open` | The relations and recurrences bin/r30 discover --window 256 --degree 2 finds on the committed basis beyond the register are candidates for deduction: measured on the window and reported, never asserted. | bin/r30 discover --window 256 --degree 2 |

## engine

| ID | Level | Statement | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `engine-workload` | `build` | Engine.lex.tex declares the workload as data (the workflow, its triggers: a schedule at minutes 17 and 47, dispatch, and pushes of the engine's inputs to main; one concurrency group that never cancels a run; runs-on ubuntu-24.04; timeout 340 minutes; permissions contents and actions write; the one secret GITHUB_TOKEN; the actions it uses; the stages of a tick with their budgets; the cache families), and the kernel decides that no secret but GITHUB_TOKEN is read, that the permissions are exactly contents and actions with write, that the stage budgets fill the tick budget and with the setup fit the timeout, that the gate keeps its share, that the cron minutes are off the hour and thirty minutes apart, that there is one concurrency group, and that every action used is one the repository already used; api sync renders .github/workflows/engine.yml from that data (guarded by the repository and the kill switch R30_ENGINE) and api check refuses drift, a secret other than GITHUB_TOKEN, an action beyond those already used, or a pull_request trigger. | bin/r30 api check; bin/r30 verify api --modules src/Engine.lex.tex; scripts/tests/test_engine.py |
| `engine-tick` | `build` | bin/r30 engine tick [--budget-minutes N] [--commit] [--push] runs one deterministic cycle from a clean checkout: it records the base commit, builds the library, runs induction (sequences --write only when the evaluation program or the κ-labels of the modules it imports changed, discover --write at the committed window), pruning (audit --write), deduction (deduce within the remaining budget) and learning (learnAll over the tick's outcomes, api sync), splits the budget across the stages from their measured durations in the ledger (the gate's own duration measured by the next tick from the commit's time) with the gate's share reserved and never cut, ends idle without a commit when nothing changed (the workflow then marks the commit settled, as it does a refused or failed tick, and later runs on it stop after the checkout), commits in the foreground through the unchanged pre-commit gate (commit --wait) and pushes only when origin/main still is the base, dropping the work otherwise; never a force push. | scripts/tests/test_engine.py |
| `engine-status` | `build` | bin/r30 engine status prints the last tick (start, base, stages with seconds and allowances, counts, outcome), the network (units: the basis sequences; synapses: the observed, proved and refuted relations; events: the ticks), the attempts by outcome, the pending attempts and the learned weights; the workflow appends it to the job summary. | scripts/tests/test_engine.py |
| `deduce-command` | `build` | bin/r30 deduce [--budget-minutes N] [--claims ids] [--dry-run] attempts every observed claim for all t with the portfolio in the learned order: each attempt renders one theorem from a template into a scratch file under .r30/deduce, checks it with one Lean process and accepts it only when its axioms are among propext and Quot.sound; accepted theorems are appended to Rule30UOR.Deduced and built; one whose statement κ a library theorem already has is removed again and the claim is proved by that library theorem (outcome known: no statement is proved twice, kappa --duplicates prints no group), the others are published (theorem add) and recorded (frontier set --status proved --lean); a relation the orbit of the diagonals breaks beyond its window is refuted by a decided counterexample. | bin/r30 deduce; bin/r30 frontier check; scripts/tests/test_engine.py |
| `strategy-portfolio` | `build` | The portfolio is four deterministic Lean proof templates under tools/r30/templates, each pinned in Engine.lex.tex by the SHA-256 of its file and of the renderer that fills it (deduce.py): library-rewrite (the columns rewritten into the diagonals, one rule step unfolded, the library's equalities among the involved constants from mentions and the register's proved relations instantiated, closed by Boolean case analysis; a publishable library theorem that states the relation proves the claim with no new theorem, outcome known), step-induction (the diagonals the relation reads as a finite system stepped by the rule, the orbit decided by the kernel), period-reduction (the words of the right system read from the row register modulo their period 2^j) and counterexample; every applicable template's Boolean core is decided in Python first. | bin/r30 api check; scripts/tests/test_engine.py |
| `strategy-learning` | `build` | Engine.lex.tex declares the learning layer: integer strategy weights per relation family, the bounded Hebbian rule learn (a success raises the weight by 2, a failure lowers it by 1, clamped to [1, 16]), learnAll and the scheduler schedule (applicable strategies by weight, ties by portfolio order) as production roots exported to certified Rust; the kernel decides that learn keeps every weight in bounds, that the committed weights are in bounds, that the schedule of every subset of the portfolio in every family is a permutation ordered by weight, and the fixtures the Python mirror computes; the tests compare the mirror with the certified roots. | bin/r30 verify api --modules src/Engine.lex.tex; scripts/tests/test_engine.py |
| `engine-ledger` | `build` | rule30-api/model/engine.toml (r30/engine/1) is the engine's ledger: the consolidated weights, every attempt (claim, κ-label, strategy, template digest, family, outcome proved, known, refuted, failed or timeout, failure point, seconds, theorem, tick) and the last ticks; no (claim κ, strategy, template digest) is attempted twice, and the weights are reproducible from the attempts. | scripts/tests/test_engine.py |
